prompt:
Image 1 is the approved visual target for this game's cast: an anime cel-shaded character with a 2px dark indigo ink outline, flat 2-3 tone shading with a hard light terminator, a single key light from the upper-left, cool ambient fill, and a fixed three-quarter view from above (camera about 55 degrees above the horizon).

TASK: Draw ONE new creature for the same game, in exactly that same visual system and camera. Match Image 1's rendering style, outline weight, shading model, light direction and level of detail precisely.

SUBJECT: a fast melee wraith called a shade.

SILHOUETTE - THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT REQUIREMENT. The creature must be ABOUT AS WIDE AS IT IS TALL, filling a roughly square area and touching all four sides of that square. A previous attempt was drawn tall and narrow and became an unreadable smudge at the size the game draws it, so width is essential. Build the width like this: a hunched, forward-leaning torso with BOTH arms thrown out wide to the left and right, ending in long spread claws; a tattered ragged cloak flaring HORIZONTALLY outward from the shoulders into long torn streamers on both sides; a ragged hem of torn cloth spreading wide at the bottom. The overall shape should be a wide spiky star or bat-like spread, with empty gaps between the arms, the cloak streamers and the body so the silhouette stays ragged and readable rather than one solid mass.

DETAIL: a dark hood with a black hollow inside and two small glowing pale eyes; deep crimson and blackened-burgundy cloth with dull bone-white trim. No legs, no feet - the hem dissolves into torn cloth and wisps.

TECHNICAL OUTPUT: square canvas, TRANSPARENT background (real alpha channel), single isolated creature, centred, with the widest parts reaching close to the left and right edges and the top and bottom close to the top and bottom edges. Fill the frame in BOTH directions.

EXCLUDE: a tall thin vertical shape, a narrow column, cast shadows on the ground, ground plane, scenery, props, other characters, text, labels, UI, frames, watermark, signature, cropped limbs, motion blur.

TASK: Draw ONE new creature for the same game, in exactly that same visual system and camera. Match Image 1's rendering style, outline weight, shading model, light direction and level of detail precisely.

SUBJECT: a floating ranged spirit called a wisp.

SILHOUETTE - THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT REQUIREMENT. The creature must be ABOUT AS WIDE AS IT IS TALL, filling a roughly square area and touching all four sides of that square. A previous attempt was drawn tall and narrow and became an unreadable smudge at the size the game draws it, so width is essential.

Build it as a SINGLE BIG ROUND BALL OF FLAME: a fat, wide teardrop body, clearly wider than it is tall in its lower half, with a large dark hollow void in the middle of the front like an empty face. Flame tongues must lick OUTWARD to the left and right sides, not upward - horizontal flame ribbons, plus two or three flat flame tips curling sideways. Any small floating shards must be tucked in tight against the left and right sides of the flame body, INSIDE its width, so that nothing sticks out above the top or below the bottom of the main body.

IMPORTANT: do not let anything extend the creature's total height - the top of the creature is the top of the flame body and the bottom is the bottom of the flame body. Keep the whole silhouette compact and round.

DETAIL: saturated violet and pale lilac flame over a darker indigo core, with the hollow centre reading almost black.

TECHNICAL OUTPUT: square canvas, TRANSPARENT background (real alpha channel), single isolated creature, centred, filling the frame in BOTH directions.

EXCLUDE: a tall thin vertical shape, a narrow column, upward-trailing flame tails, cast shadows on the ground, ground plane, scenery, props, other characters, text, labels, UI, frames, watermark, signature, cropped shapes, motion blur.
